quotes.text: I think AI presents a lot of opportunity. There are a lot of good things that you can do with AI. But I also think that we need some sort of common-sense guardrails on it, and I think that’s going to be really important.

From an economic standpoint, there are going to be a lot of folks who are going to be out of work because AI has the potential to take over their jobs. And if we’re not taking a future-thinking approach to that, and thinking about how we start providing real training opportunities and support for people who might have to rethink their career choices, I think we’re going to have a lot of people who fall through the cracks.

This again goes to: We need more energy. There’s more need for energy and for this kind of power in the world and in the state. But we also have an aging power grid in Nebraska, and folks are already feeling their energy costs go up, and now we’ve got gas prices going up.

It's important that we continue to lead in this space, but not without taking into consideration the broader impacts on our community. That's where guardrails come in — independent investigations, more transparency, and proposals like requiring a kill switch.
When you have all the major CEOs of every AI company basically going to the United Nations and asking for regulation, we should listen.
